description:
It all started with a shared curiosity about space and an idea that grew into GASD.XP! We're from the UAE, creating a space mission game where players design spacecraft, manage resources and explore challenges.

Using the Design Thinking Process, our team combines creativity and engineering:
• Aditi–Plans mission objectives, strategies and orbits.
• Gurudharsini–Designs spacecraft systems and manages resources.
• Deeksha–Develops the game, interface and interactive features.
summary:
GASD.XP (Galactic Aerospace Simulation and Design) is an interactive space mission design and simulation game where players will be able to see how difficult the process of designing a space mission may be. We came up with the idea of the game with three missions: a Mars Rover Mission, a Moon Landing Mission and an Asteroid Mining Probe Mission.

The player will be able to customize their spacecraft, choose scientific instruments, pick launch vehicles and manage various resources, which include budget, mass, power, fuel and communications. The decisions will affect the performance of the mission, making players analyze the process and see the engineering challenges behind the missions. 

GASD.XP provides the solution to the challenge by turning the space mission planning into an interactive process. It is significant because it helps make the concepts of aerospace science more accessible, inspires scientific interest, helps develop critical thinking and decision-making skills of the players.
details:
Our Project Solution

GASD.XP (Galactic Aerospace Simulation & Design.XP) is an interactive educational platform that introduces students to space exploration, astronomy and aerospace engineering through games and simulations.

When we think about space exploration, we often picture rockets launching or astronauts travelling to other planets. However, there is much more involved in planning a space mission. Engineers have to consider spacecraft mass, fuel, power supply, communication systems, scientific instruments, mission objectives and available budgets. Even a small change in one of these factors can affect the entire mission.

We wanted to make these concepts easier for students to understand, especially those who have never had the opportunity to experiment with spacecraft design. This led us to develop GASD.XP, where players can explore space, plan missions, make engineering decisions and see how their choices affect the results.

Instead of learning everything through written explanations, players get to interact with the concepts themselves. The platform brings together mission simulations, interactive space environments, mini-games, quizzes, weekly challenges, leaderboards and achievements, along with a Space Academy and Help Centre.

How Does Our Solution Work?

GASD.XP brings different space-related activities together in one platform. Each section introduces players to a different aspect of space science and exploration.

1. Space Mission Design and Simulation

The mission design system is one of the main features of GASD.XP. Players take on the role of aerospace engineers and plan missions by choosing spacecraft components, scientific instruments and launch systems.

However, they cannot simply select every available component. Each choice comes with certain requirements and limitations.

Players have to consider several factors during mission planning.

Mass and Payload Capacity: The spacecraft must remain within the payload capacity of its launch vehicle. If its mass exceeds the permitted limit, the launch can fail.

Power Management: Scientific instruments require electricity to operate. Players must make sure their total power requirements do not exceed the available supply.

Mission Budget: Each mission has a limited number of credits. Players have to decide which components are necessary and how much they can spend.

Launch Vehicles: Different launch vehicles are suited to different missions. Choosing an appropriate vehicle is important for reaching the intended destination.

Scientific Instruments: Players select instruments based on what they want to investigate. Each instrument has its own mass and power requirements.

Communication Systems: Collecting scientific information is only part of a mission. Spacecraft must also be able to transmit their findings back to Earth.

Mission Objectives: The purpose of each mission influences the spacecraft design and the components required.

These requirements make mission planning more than just selecting components. Players have to think about how their choices work together and make changes when their design does not meet the mission requirements.

2. Multiple Space Missions

GASD.XP includes different missions to introduce players to various types of space exploration.

Mars Rover Mission

Players experience the challenges of operating a rover on Mars. They navigate the Martian surface, manage available energy, locate scientific investigation points, analyse discoveries and transmit collected information.

This mission introduces rover operations, scientific exploration, energy management and communication limitations.

Moon Landing Mission

Players explore the requirements involved in planning a lunar landing mission. They learn about spacecraft design, launch systems and the challenges associated with reaching and exploring the Moon.

Asteroid Mining Probe

Inspired by real asteroid exploration missions such as NASA's OSIRIS-REx, this mission introduces players to asteroid exploration and spacecraft operations in a distant environment.

Each mission offers a different experience and allows players to explore how mission requirements change depending on the destination and objectives.

3. Interactive Space Environments and Orbital Activities

We also wanted players to explore space beyond the individual missions.

GASD.XP includes interactive space environments and orbital activities that introduce concepts such as orbital motion, celestial objects and planetary environments. Players can explore how objects move in space and become more familiar with astronomical concepts through visual interaction.

This gives students an opportunity to understand topics that can sometimes be difficult to imagine through textbooks alone.

4. Space Mini-Games

The platform includes several space-themed mini-games involving exploration, navigation, observation, coordination and logical reasoning.

These activities provide another way to interact with space-related concepts and allow players to practise their knowledge without having to complete a full mission simulation every time.

5. Interactive Quizzes

Quizzes test players' understanding of astronomy, space science and aerospace-related topics. They can use them to check what they have learned through the different activities and practise recalling information instead of simply reading educational material.

6. Weekly Challenges

Weekly challenges introduce additional objectives for players to complete. They add variety to the platform and give players new reasons to explore different activities and improve their performance.

7. Leaderboards and Competitive Learning

GASD.XP includes a leaderboard where players can compare their scores and achievements. This adds a competitive element to the learning experience and encourages them to participate in different activities and challenge themselves.

8. Awards and Achievements

The awards and achievements section recognises players' progress across the platform. Players can work towards unlocking achievements by exploring different features and completing activities, giving them additional goals beyond finishing individual missions.

9. Space Academy and Help Centre

We included a Space Academy to support players who want to learn more about space related topics.

The Help Centre provides guidance on using the platform, understanding its features and learning the game controls. These sections are particularly useful for beginners who may be unfamiliar with aerospace engineering or the different activities available.

10. Player Profiles and Accessibility

GASD.XP includes optional login and registration functionality. Players can explore the platform without being required to create an account, while those who choose to register can access profile-related features.

We also considered how students would use the platform on different devices. Computer users can navigate the games using keyboard controls, including arrow keys, while mobile and tablet users can use virtual touch controls. The interface is designed to adjust to different screen sizes.

We wanted the platform to be straightforward to navigate so players could spend more time exploring and less time figuring out how to use it.

The Benefits of Our Project

GASD.XP offers students a way to explore aerospace engineering and space science through practical activities rather than relying entirely on theoretical explanations.

It makes STEM learning more engaging by introducing scientific concepts through games, simulations and interactive environments. It also develops problem-solving skills because players have to find solutions while working within limitations involving mass, power, budgets and mission requirements.

Students get an introduction to the decisions involved in designing and managing spacecraft. They can experiment with different choices, understand how engineering decisions influence mission outcomes and develop an interest in scientific exploration.

The platform also supports independent learning, allowing players to explore different sections at their own pace. Quizzes, leaderboards, weekly challenges and achievements provide additional motivation to participate and improve.

What Makes Our Project Creative?

What makes GASD.XP different is the way it brings several aspects of space education together in one platform.

We did not want to create just another space themed quiz or a game where players simply travel between planets. We wanted them to understand some of the thinking that takes place behind actual space missions.

For example, a player designing a spacecraft might want to include several scientific instruments. However, adding more instruments also affects the spacecraft's mass and power requirements. The player then has to decide which instruments are worth including while staying within the mission's limitations.

Similarly, the mission budget means that players cannot always choose every component they want. They have to prioritise what is necessary for their objectives.

These interactions allow players to experience how different engineering requirements are connected rather than learning about each one separately.

We also combined these simulations with retro pixel-inspired visuals, interactive space environments, mini-games, quizzes and competitive features. Players can move between different activities depending on what they want to explore.

Our aim was to make the platform feel like an interactive space exploration experience while still having a clear educational purpose.

Factors Our Team Considered During Development:

While developing GASD.XP, our team had to consider both the scientific content and the experience of the people using the platform.

One of our main considerations was scientific relevance. We wanted the missions to introduce concepts connected to real space exploration rather than making them entirely fictional. This influenced our inclusion of spacecraft mass, payload capacity, power requirements, mission budgets, launch vehicle suitability, scientific instruments and communication systems.

We also considered how these factors would affect one another. For instance, adding an instrument changes the spacecraft's mass and power requirements, which may affect whether the mission design is suitable.

Another challenge was deciding how to present these concepts to younger students. We wanted the simulations to introduce meaningful engineering decisions without becoming too complicated for beginners.

We also thought about the variety of activities needed to keep the platform interesting, the clarity of game instructions, keyboard and touch controls, navigation and compatibility across different devices.

Balancing educational value, technical requirements and ease of use was an important part of developing GASD.XP.

Our Goal and Intended Impact:

Our main goal is to make space science and aerospace engineering more accessible to younger students.

Not everyone gets the opportunity to experiment with spacecraft design or understand how a space mission is planned. Through GASD.XP, we want to give students a way to explore these ideas, even if they have little or no previous knowledge of aerospace engineering.

We hope the platform encourages students to ask questions, test different possibilities and think about the science behind space exploration.

In the longer term, we want GASD.XP to encourage more students to explore STEM subjects, increase awareness of aerospace engineering, make difficult scientific concepts easier to understand and introduce students to careers in astronomy, engineering and scientific research.

Ultimately, we want students to see space exploration as more than something they watch from Earth. We want them to understand the decisions behind it and experience some of the challenges involved in making a mission possible.

Tools and Technologies Used

Development Platform

Base44 was used as our AI-assisted website development platform to build the GASD.XP website and develop its features.

AI-Assisted Development

AI-assisted tools supported parts of the website development process, including website structuring, feature development and refinement.

Web Development Technologies

HTML was used for structuring web content.

CSS was used for styling, visual presentation and responsive layouts.

JavaScript was used for interactive functionality and game-related logic.

Design Approach

The platform uses a retro pixel-inspired visual design with space-themed interfaces, interactive game elements, animations and responsive layouts for different screen sizes.
